subject: Post-demo: inference fit recommendations + JSON-schema/tool-calling next steps
messages:

Cc: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>

Subject: Post-demo: inference fit recommendations + JSON-schema/tool-calling next steps

Hi Olivia / Calliope team — thanks again for hopping on the demo this morning. Quick recap and suggested next steps so we can get a focused technical follow-up scheduled.

Recap (what you said you care about)
- Primary workload: structured extraction from customer emails and routing to downstream order system (must emit exact JSON for downstream parser).
- SLOs: p95 latency target ~300ms / turn; peak concurrent throughput ~20 rps.
- Quality: schema compliance (no missing required fields), low hallucination on item lists, and deterministic order routing decisions.
- Constraint: on-prem deployment possibility later this year; initially prefer hosted with reserved capacity.

Initial model-fit recommendations (fast shortlist)
- mistral-7b-instruct (v1.1): strong structured-output behavior at low latency; great for JSON-heavy extract tasks.
- rdw-13b-q4f16 (Redwood-verified quantized): better accuracy for longer context when you need entity extraction + summaries.
- fallback: gpt-compat-3.5-small (cost-effective, useful for retries / simple cases).

Why these: we prioritized models that are known to (a) comply with JSON schema when prompted with a strict schema + examples, and (b) have predictable latency on our dedicated pools. We'll run a focused eval to validate exact_match rates for the schema.

Tool/function-calling considerations
- Define a canonical JSON schema for the "order_action" payload (required fields: order_id, customer_id, items[], routing_code). We'll attach a suggested schema file in the prompt set.
- Use function-calling mode to force structured outputs where possible and include a strong "validation-first" prompt pattern (example prompts attached in prompt_set_v1.jsonl).
- Retries: recommend idempotency keys on your side (request_id) so model retries can be retried safely. Redwood can be configured to do automatic small-model fallback on transient errors.

Proposed quick evaluation plan (what we'll run before deep technical call)
- We'll run 600 labeled prompts from your prompt_set_v1.jsonl across the two model candidates and produce: schema_exact_match, field_level_precision/recall, avg_latency, 99th_latency, and hallucination_rate (items not present in input).
- Thresholds to check: schema_exact_match >= 95%; avg_latency <= 350ms on dedicated pool for mistral-7b; hallucination_rate < 3% for item lists.

Attachments: post-demo-slides.pdf (slides), prompt_set_v1.jsonl (sample prompts/examples), benchmarks-calliope-20260618.csv (placeholder baseline).

Next steps (proposed)
1) Share your red team prompt examples + 24 sample emails (we can plug into the harness).
2) Rishi to run baseline eval on mistral-7b-instruct + rdw-13b-q4f16 and share results within 48 hours.
3) Schedule 60-min tech deep-dive next week to review failures and fallback strategy (please share preferred time windows).

If that all sounds good I'll kick off the baseline runs and send calendar invites.

—

Thanks Vanessa — great recap and appreciate the clear plan. A few clarifying questions before you run the baseline: 

1) Hallucination definition: when you say "hallucination_rate < 3% for item lists", how are you measuring it (false positives only, or missing items too)? We have some noisy parses in our annotation set and want to align definitions.

2) JSON schema enforcement: we saw in a sandbox that sometimes the model emits a valid JSON but with incorrect data types (e.g., item.quantity as string). Do you validate types server-side or rely on model prompting + function-calling?

3) Costs: can you give a rough per-1k-token cost estimate for the two candidate models on a reserved capacity plan? We need that for procurement.

We can share 24 labeled emails by EOD and a small red-team set (10 tricky examples).

Also, Tuesday or Wednesday next week looks good for the deep-dive.

- Olivia

Subject: Re: Post-demo: inference fit recommendations + JSON-schema/tool-calling next steps

Hi Olivia — quick technical notes to answer your questions and set expectations for the baseline run.

On hallucination measurement
- We'll report two metrics: false_positive_rate (items the model invented) and false_negative_rate (items present in source that model missed). Your "hallucination_rate" can be defined as false_positive_rate. We'll include both so you can judge tradeoffs.

On JSON schema / data types
- Recommended approach: function-calling + model prompt constraint + server-side validation. The flow we plan to run: 
  1) Request -> model.function_call (returns structured payload)
  2) Redwood validation layer (fast schema check): parses JSON, validates types & required fields. If validation fails, we do up to 2 automated repair attempts with temperature 0 and an augmented prompt that includes the validation error.
  3) If still invalid, we mark as failure and return the model string response to a small repair microservice (this can be a cheaper small model or a deterministic parser).

- This strategy keeps downstream deterministic and reduces silent type errors. We'll log schema_failure_reason for each failed case.

On retries / idempotency
- Use client-supplied request_id (UUID) so retries are idempotent. Redwood will attach retry_count and last_model_used in trace metadata. For transient infra errors we use exponential backoff (100ms * 2^n) with max 3 retries.

On cost estimates (rough for reserved capacity)
- mistral-7b-instruct: ~ $0.80 per 1k tokens (estimate on dedicated pool).
- rdw-13b-q4f16: ~ $1.90 per 1k tokens (higher, but more accurate on extraction tasks).
- small fallback model: ~ $0.15 per 1k tokens.
(These are estimates — procurement will need a formal pricing sheet; Vanessa will loop in sales ops if Calliope wants committed capacity.)

Baseline eval specifics we'll produce in the CSV: schema_exact_match, field_precision, field_recall, false_positive_rate, false_negative_rate, avg_latency_ms, p95_latency_ms, model_tokens_consumed. We'll also produce a per-example failure reason column (e.g., "missing_required_field:items", "type_mismatch:quantity").

I'll kick off the runs once Vanessa confirms and we have the 24 labeled emails. If you can also provide a red-team set of 10 tricky cases we'll run those with temperature sweeps (0, 0.2, 0.5) to find the sweet spot for accuracy vs. safety.

-Rishi
